settlementFee.note: CENTRAL STRUCTURAL FINDING: DTIRB's Rating Manual is, like Ohio's OTIRB, a 'no carve-out needed' unregulated-settlement-fee state. Section 1.5 defines 'Rate(s)' as being 'for title insurance premiums related to coverage in policies and endorsements, and do not include charges for searches, abstracts, attorney's fees, escrow or closing services or other services charged by attorneys, abstractors, etc.' Section 2.1 restates this: 'The Rates herein quoted are for title insurance premium only and do not include charges for searches, abstracts, Commitments, attorney's fees, or settlement/closing fees. Nothing contained herein shall preclude either Insurer or Agent from imposing charges ancillary to the issuance of a title insurance policy.' This is the exact unregulated territory the task brief targeted -- settlement/closing/escrow/attorney fees are fully market-set in Delaware, for every provider type, with no promulgated settlement-fee number comparable to NJ's NJLTIRB Article 6. DTIRB's 16 current members (as of 04/01/2025) include all five national underwriters named in the task brief -- Chicago Title, Fidelity National Title, First American Title, Old Republic National Title, and Stewart Title Guaranty -- plus WFG National Title, Commonwealth Land Title, Conestoga Title, Doma Title, First National Title, Investors Title, AmTrust Title, Agents National Title, National Title Insurance of New York, The Security Title Guarantee Corporation of Baltimore, and Title Resources Guaranty.
settlementFee.simultaneousIssueSurcharge: $25.00 simultaneous-issue rate when a Homeowner's/Owner's Policy and an Expanded Coverage Loan Policy are issued simultaneously on the same property (Section 3.12)
settlementFee.closingProtectionLetter: $125.00 per transaction, regardless of the number of letters issued for a single transaction (single-transaction CPL); remitted entirely to the Insurer, not the Agent or Approved Attorney (Section 6.1)

itemizedFees.docPrep: NOT regulated by the Manual -- Sections 1.5 and 2.1 explicitly exclude attorney's fees and settlement/closing charges from the Rate; no DTIRB-set figure

itemizedFees.searchExam: Explicitly excluded from the Rate by Section 1.5 ('do not include charges for searches, abstracts, attorney's fees, escrow or closing services') -- title search/examination fees in Delaware are typically the closing attorney's or title agent's own charge, not DTIRB-rated
itemizedFees.cpl: $125.00 per transaction, single-transaction letter, remitted entirely to the Insurer (Section 6.1) -- see settlementFee.closingProtectionLetter above

bundlingNotes: DTIRB's Sections 1.5 and 2.1 are the most direct 'premium-only' unregulated-settlement-fee language found in this survey outside of Ohio's GP-4 -- Delaware's rating bureau declares up front that searches, abstracts, attorney's fees, escrow, and closing/settlement charges are never part of the regulated premium for any provider type (Insurer or Agent). Because Delaware additionally requires a Delaware-licensed attorney to conduct every residential closing and disburse funds (an attorney-closing-state custom distinct from DTIRB regulation itself, confirmed via multiple independent sources -- see DE.md), the entire settlement/service-fee stack the task brief targeted is priced by whichever attorney or title/settlement agency handles the file, not by the Manual. The one closing-adjacent item DTIRB does price is the Closing Protection Letter at a flat $125.00/transaction (Section 6.1), remitted entirely to the Insurer.
transactionContext: Applies uniformly statewide (New Castle, Kent, and Sussex Counties alike) to all DTIRB member insurers' and agents' Owner's and Loan policy premiums; no purchase-vs-refinance distinction in the base rate.

bundlingNotes: This is the single genuine provider-published, dollar-denominated Delaware settlement/attorney-fee figure located this session. It illustrates Delaware's attorney-closing custom directly: because DTIRB's own Manual excludes attorney's fees and settlement/closing charges from the regulated premium (see the DTIRB entry above), and Delaware law requires a licensed Delaware attorney to conduct the settlement and disburse funds, the closing-attorney's bundled fee IS the settlement-fee market signal in Delaware, rather than a separate title-company line item layered on top of an independent attorney fee (contrast NJ, where both a regulated title-company settlement charge and an additive, unregulated attorney fee exist side by side). The $1,400-$1,600 range bundles title exam, attorney review, settlement coordination, admin, and transaction coordination into one number rather than itemizing doc prep/wire/courier/notary separately, consistent with the market-opacity pattern (bundled rather than itemized pricing) observed at attorney-run firms in other states surveyed (e.g., NJ's Makarov and Y. Levin flat fees).
